issues.description: setuptools<82 pinned as a runtime dependency in core/setup.py complects CI workaround with user-facing install contract
issues.detail: The pin lives in the CI scripts because mmcv's build is broken on setuptools>=82. Putting the same cap into core/setup.py's install_requires propagates a transient upstream bug into every downstream environment that installs autogluon.core, regardless of whether they ever touch mmcv. Build-time tooling and runtime dependencies are different concerns; this conflates them.

issues.description: The fix encodes three independent version constraints in three different places with no shared source of truth
issues.detail: setuptools<82 now appears in env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh, and core/setup.py, each with its own FIXME or none. When the upstream mmcv issue resolves, a future maintainer must find and revert three separated places. The version constraint is a value; it should live in one named place that the three call sites reference.

issues.description: mmdet bumped from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 with no stated reason alongside an unrelated build fix
issues.detail: The PR is titled as a CI fix for mmengine, but it also moves mmdet a minor version and switches mmengine from a pinned git SHA to a PyPI release. These are three separate decisions braided into one diff. Reviewers cannot tell which version change is load-bearing for the build and which is incidental drift.

issues.description: Redundant setuptools<82 install inside setup_mmcv.sh duplicates what build_pkg already established
issues.detail: build_pkg in env_setup.sh now upgrades setuptools<82, and setup_mmcv.sh re-pins it on its own line. If the environment contract is that setuptools is already constrained globally for CI, the second pin is incidental noise. If it isn't, the first pin is insufficient. Pick one place and name what it owns.

issues.description: FIXME comments name a symptom but not the condition for reversal
issues.detail: Both FIXMEs point at mmcv issue 3325 and say 'remove cap once fixed.' The actual revert condition is more specific: mmcv 2.1.0 (or whatever version is pinned) must publish a wheel or sdist that builds under setuptools>=82. Without naming that, the next maintainer must re-derive it. The condition is a value; write it down.

review.summary: The change unbraids a real CI break (setuptools 82 removing pkg_resources, which mmcv's build relies on) by pinning setuptools<82 and switching mmengine off a git SHA onto a PyPI release. That's a reasonable workaround, but it complects three separate concerns in one diff: the build-tool pin, the mmcv/mmengine/mmdet version bumps, and a runtime install_requires change in core/setup.py. The most important decomplection is pulling setuptools<82 out of core/setup.py — that's a CI value leaking into the user-facing install contract. The version cap also lives in three places with no shared source of truth, which guarantees a partial revert when upstream fixes mmcv 3325.
